articles.label: Install on Windows
articles.title: Install, upgrade and uninstall Vivary on Windows
articles.description: Download the Vivary Windows installer, verify its checksum, install it without administrator rights, then upgrade, back up, or uninstall it.
articles.summary: Install Vivary for your Windows account with the setup program, or use the optional portable ZIP. Then upgrade, back up, or remove it.

articles.label: Runtimes and keys
articles.title: Set up coding runtimes and provider keys
articles.description: Connect Claude Code or Codex to Vivary, choose Codex permissions, and add the provider keys that Native chat and automation conditions use.
articles.summary: Code conversations run Claude Code or Codex, which you install and sign in to yourself. Native chat and automation conditions use API keys that you add in Settings.

articles.label: Projects
articles.title: Open and set up projects
articles.description: Open a folder or create a project in Vivary, set up an existing folder, reconnect a moved folder, and work with Files, search, health and Memory.
articles.summary: A project is a folder on your computer that Vivary and your agents work in. Open a folder you already have, or create a new project.

articles.label: Conversations
articles.title: Work in conversations
articles.description: Start Code conversations and Native chats in Vivary, choose a runtime and model, stop a run, link conversations, archive chats and search history.
articles.summary: Each project keeps its own conversations. A Code conversation runs Claude Code or Codex. A Native chat runs on the provider key you added.

articles.label: Handoffs
articles.title: Save a handoff to STATE.md
articles.description: Use Prepare handoff and Save handoff in Vivary to record goals, decisions and next steps in a project's state document, and keep that record current.
articles.summary: A handoff records where the work stands in the project's state document, such as STATE.md, so the next session or agent can pick it up from the file.

articles.label: Automations
articles.title: Run automations
articles.description: Create Vivary automations that run on a schedule, an event or a local webhook, run them now, approve protected actions, and review file changes.
articles.summary: An automation is a saved instruction that the agent runs on a schedule, on an event, when a program calls its webhook, or when you choose Run now.

articles.label: Remote access
articles.title: Open Vivary on another device
articles.description: Turn on Vivary remote access over a protected HTTPS connection you already run, pair a browser on another device, and revoke or disable access.
articles.summary: Remote access lets a browser on another device open the Vivary that runs on this computer. It is off until you turn it on and pair each browser.

articles.label: Troubleshooting
articles.title: Troubleshoot Vivary
articles.description: Fix common Vivary problems: installer messages, launch failures, runtimes that are not ready, unavailable projects, stuck runs and automation errors.
articles.summary: Find the symptom you see, then follow its action. Each table covers one part of Vivary.
